language.script_notes: Balinese script appears decoratively on temple gates and cultural signage in Bali specifically — a strong regional tell where visible.
false_friends: Java (shares volcanic terrain and Javanese-descended Hindu temple architectural roots)

road_furniture.curb_style: Small stone/woven offering baskets (canang sari) placed on the ground outside doorways and shopfronts are a near-unique Bali-specific tell.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Small roadside Hindu shrines are common in Bali specifically.

architecture.roof_style: Multi-tiered thatched meru towers (pagoda-like shrine roofs) are Bali's single strongest architectural tell; elsewhere in Nusa Tenggara, simpler vernacular construction predominates.
architecture.roof_material: Layered black palm-fiber thatch (ijuk) on meru towers and temple roofs in Bali; corrugated metal more common further east in Nusa Tenggara's poorer, drier islands.
architecture.wall_construction: Balinese pura (Hindu temples) built as a series of walled courtyards with an iconic split gate (candi bentar) entrance; carved volcanic-stone temple facades; simpler, more sparsely developed villages further east on Lombok, Flores, Sumba and Timor.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Grey-black volcanic stone temple carving in Bali; simpler earth-toned village construction further east.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Balinese Hindu temples (pura) with split gates and tiered meru towers; terraced rice paddies (subak irrigation system) with small shrines beside them; the Komodo dragon habitat and dry savanna landscape further east on Flores/Komodo.

nature.vegetation: Lush, intensively irrigated terraced rice paddies and tropical vegetation in Bali; increasingly dry monsoon forest and open savanna woodland moving east through Lombok, Sumbawa, Flores, Sumba and Timor — among the driest, most seasonal landscapes in Indonesia.
nature.terrain: Volcanic peaks and terraced hillsides in Bali (Mount Agung, Mount Batur); a chain of smaller volcanic islands continuing east, becoming progressively drier and less forested, home to Komodo National Park's savanna landscape.
nature.climate_signature: Bali itself is lush and humid; the islands further east (Nusa Tenggara proper) are noticeably drier and browner with savanna rather than rainforest — a strong within-region gradient worth knowing.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Very heavy scooter/motorbike traffic in Bali's tourist areas; simpler, sparser vehicle presence further east in rural Nusa Tenggara.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Good coverage in Bali (a major tourist destination); much sparser across Lombok, Flores, Sumba and Timor.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Bali is well covered; the rest of Nusa Tenggara has real, significant coverage gaps.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Volcanic terrain, rice terraces, shared Hindu-influenced temple architectural roots
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Bali's temples have the distinctive split gate (candi bentar) and tiered meru towers of Hindu architecture; Java is predominantly Muslim with pyramidal-roofed mosques instead, and Balinese canang sari offering baskets are absent in Java.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Tropical Buddhist/Hindu temple imagery can superficially resemble Balinese architecture to an untrained eye
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Bali drives on the left with Indonesian plates and Balinese-script temple signage; Thailand's temple architecture (wat, chedi) and script are entirely different, and Thailand also drives on the left but with completely different plate and signage conventions.
